sentences.text: Shri Ajay Raj Gupta - Advocate for the applicant.
Shri Kushagra Jain - Dy.G.A for the respondent/State.

Order 
This is Second bail application under Section 439 of Cr.P.C/Section 483 of BNSS for grant of regular bail in connection with crime No.557/2023 dated : not mentioned, registered at P.S. - Khudel,
District - Indore for offences punishable under Sections 363, 366, 376(2)(n), 376(2)(F) of IPC and Section 5(L)/6 of POCSO Act.
The first bail application was dismissed as withdrawn with liberty to file fresh application after the Court statement of the prosecutrix.
The present application is filed mainly on the ground that the prosecutrix is not turning up in the witness box.
2. Counsel for the State was granted time on 26/11/2024, 2/12/2024 and 9/12/2024 to ascertain the fact that why the prosecutrix is not turning up.

He produced a report from the police station Khudel,
District Indore.
According to the said report, the prosecutrix has not appeared even on the last date i.e 6/12/2024.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:35441 2 MCRC-48449-2024 3.
Counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is in jail since 14/1/2024 and is aged about only 20 years.
According to the prosecution story, the prosecutrix had eloped with the applicant on 22/9/2023.

He relied on the statement of the prosecutrix recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C and submits that from the aforesaid statement it is clear that she herself had gone alongwith the accused to Sendhwa and then to Gujarat where she lived with him for about two months and made physical relationship with him.

sentences.text: Counsel for the State opposes the prayer and submits that as per the scholar register, the age of the prosecutrix is 14 years and, therefore, the application be rejected.

5. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and taking into consideration the previous order passed by this Court in the earlier bail application and also the fact that the prosecutrix is not turning up in the witness box.
The applicant is aged about 20 years and it would not be in the interest of justice to keep him in jail for a long time.
He is jail since 14.1.2024.
In view of the aforesaid, this Court is of the considered opinion that the applicant is entitled for grant of bail.

6. It is directed that applicant Sunil shall be released from custody upon furnishing a personal bond of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty thousand Only) with one surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the Ld. Court below.
7. A typed copy of this order is being forwarded to the Office of the Advocate General, on their email address, for intimation to the Police Station concerned.
The office is directed to forward a copy of this order to the Ld.
NEUTRAL
CITATION
NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:35441 3 MCRC-48449-2024 Court below

. 
8. With the aforesaid, the application is allowed and disposed off.
Cc as per rules.
